target.title: feat: add sessions_search transcript search
target.body:
Closes #100978

AI-assisted: yes (Codex)

## What Problem This Solves

Agents currently cannot search their own prior session transcripts when they remember a topic, decision, identifier, or phrase but do not know the exact session key or history page. That makes long-running work harder to resume and forces agents to list sessions manually, then page through histories one by one.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a first-class `sessions_search` agent tool backed by a new Gateway method, `sessions.search`, and a per-agent SQLite FTS5 transcript index. The design keeps the new capability inside the existing session-tool privacy model: agents can only search sessions they could already inspect with `sessions_history`, and no new config surface or cross-agent policy is introduced.

Technical shape:

- Agent tool surface: `sessions_search` accepts `{ query, sessionKey?, limit? }`. When `sessionKey` is omitted, the tool first calls `sessions.list` and filters rows through the same effective `tools.sessions.visibility` and agent-to-agent rules used by history/list tooling. When `sessionKey` is present, it resolves and checks the explicit target before search.
- Gateway API: `sessions.search` accepts `query`, optional `sessionKey`/`sessionKeys`, optional `agentId`, and optional `limit`. It returns bounded hits with `sessionKey`, `sessionId`, `agentId`, `seq`, `role`, `snippet`, and optional timestamp/message id so callers can follow up with `sessions_history`.
- Storage/indexing: the per-agent SQLite DB now owns `session_transcript_search_sources` plus an FTS5 virtual table. Search reconciles each targeted transcript by stat metadata (`mtime`, `size`, canonical session key) before querying, so unchanged transcripts are reused and changed transcripts are reindexed.
- Stale-row protection: replacing a session key's transcript path purges old FTS/source rows for that key before inserting the new rows, preventing search from returning snippets that current `sessions_history` would no longer show.
- Indexed content boundary: only user/assistant visible transcript text is indexed. The index strips inline directive tags, applies the existing tool-payload redaction helper, truncates large message text before indexing, and excludes tool/system/internal records.
- Query behavior: FTS queries quote whitespace-delimited terms for SQLite FTS5 `MATCH`, rank by `bm25`, and use `snippet(...)` for compact excerpts. A LIKE fallback handles FTS parser failures without widening the session scope.
- Generated/client surfaces: Gateway protocol schemas/types are exported, native Swift protocol models are regenerated, and tool display metadata plus the shared tool-display snapshot are updated.

Non-goals and boundaries:

- No new `openclaw.json` option or environment variable.
- No background watcher or persistent worker; the index is reconciled when search targets are requested.
- No cross-plugin policy in core; visibility remains delegated to the existing session-tool helpers.

## User Impact

Agents can now search visible session transcripts by phrase and get concise, redacted snippets with enough provenance to open the exact session history afterward. Users get better recall across long-running work without broadening access beyond existing session visibility rules.

## Evidence

Local validation after CI fixes:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-search-tool.test.ts` - passed 2 shards, 2 files, 8 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/native-protocol-levels.guard.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts src/state/sqlite-query-plan.test.ts` - passed 4 files, 65 tests, 1 skipped.
- `node scripts/generate-kysely-types.mjs --verify` - passed; Node reported the expected experimental SQLite warning.
- `node scripts/check-kysely-guardrails.mjs` - passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=8` - passed.
- `node --import tsx scripts/tool-display.ts --check` - passed.
- `pnpm check:architecture` - passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check` - passed after committing regenerated Swift protocol models.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` - passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` - clean after the CI-fix commit.

CI failures addressed:

- `check-lint`: fixed `no-underscore-dangle`, `unicorn/prefer-math-min-max`, and `oxc/no-map-spread` findings.
- `check-guards`: added `sessions_search` tool-display metadata and regenerated the shared snapshot.
- `check-additional-runtime-topology-architecture`: documented the FTS5 raw SQLite call sites with local `sqlite-allow-raw` comments and reran Kysely guardrails.
- `checks-fast-bundled-protocol`: regenerated Swift Gateway protocol models for `SessionsSearch*` schemas.

Known proof gap: Testbox warmup could not run locally because the available `crabbox` binary is 0.18.0 while the wrapper requires >=0.22.0 for Blacksmith Testbox, and no sibling `../crabbox` checkout was present to rebuild it. Focused local fallback tests/typecheck/guards were run instead.
